content: This medication should be used at the lowest effective dose and for the shortest duration necessary. It is important to discuss its use with your doctor and have regular follow-ups, such as every 3 to 6 months, to determine if continued use is necessary. If long-term use is required, you should undergo regular comprehensive physical exams, including annual evaluations as directed by your doctor. This medication is a hormone used by women to alleviate vaginal symptoms of menopause, such as dryness, burning, and itching, which occur due to reduced estrogen production. When treating only vaginal symptoms of menopause, products applied directly inside the vagina, like this medication, are typically recommended as the first option. Before starting this medication, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Use the medication exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Fill the applicator with the medication as directed, insert it high into the vagina, and press the plunger to release the medication. After use, clean the applicator thoroughly with warm, soapy water and rinse well. To achieve the best results, use the medication regularly and adhere to the prescribed dosing schedule. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, bloating, breast tenderness, headaches, or weight changes. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. However, in rare cases, this medication may cause serious, potentially fatal complications such as blood clots, heart attack, stroke, or clots in the lungs or legs. Severe allergic reactions to this product are also rare. If you experience any concerning symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Avoid smoking or using tobacco while on this medication, as it increases the risk of blood clots. Notify your doctor if you have recently undergone or will undergo surgery, or if you will be immobile for an extended period (e.g., during a long flight), as these conditions can elevate your risk of blood clots, especially when using estrogen products. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen or protective clothing when outdoors. If you are nearsighted or wear contact lenses, you may experience vision problems or difficulty wearing your lenses. Some estrogen products contain mineral oil, which can weaken rubber products like latex condoms, cervical caps, and diaphragms, potentially leading to their failure. This medication should not be used during pregnancy. It can pass into breast milk and may reduce the quality and quantity of milk produced. Discuss breastfeeding with your doctor before using this medication. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests, such as the metyrapone test, potentially causing inaccurate results. In the event of an overdose, this medication can be harmful if swallowed. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Lifestyle changes such as reducing stress, eating a low-fat/low-salt diet, losing weight if overweight, exercising regularly, and quitting smoking can help control or prevent these conditions. Keeping your mind active with mental exercises, such as reading or solving puzzles, may also help prevent dementia. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for guidance on safe disposal. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
